item.title: Artist known for sculptures of Mao Zedong jailed for slandering ‘heroes and martyrs’
item.description: Gao Zhen sentenced to three years in prison after already spending two years in detention Gao Zhen, a prominent Chinese artist known for provocative sculptures of the former leader Mao Zedong, has been sentenced to three years in prison after being found guilty of slandering China’s “heroes and martyrs”. The sentencing came two years after he was detained while visiting the country with his family, according to his wife and human rights groups. The case has attracted international condemnation , largely because the artworks at the centre of the case were created more than 10 years before… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: ¿Cómo los grupos armados reclutan menores por redes sociales en Colombia?
item.description: Un informe de Human Rights Watch (HRW), publicado este 24 de agosto, dejó en evidencia el aumento del reclutamiento de menores de edad por parte de grupos armados en Colombia a través de redes sociales, sobre todo por parte de las disidencias de las FARC. En France 24 hablamos con Juan Pappier, subdirector para las Américas de HRW, para determinar de qué forma se puede evitar el reclutamiento de menores en el país, además de las causas de este flagelo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Marruecos dice que los inmigrantes que entraron en Ceuta defendían que la ciudad «es marroquí»: «¿Cómo impedirles que piensen así?»

item.title: French police accused of rising use of violence to stop Channel crossings
item.description: NGO criticises ‘human cost’ of UK-funded crackdown on attempts to set off from French beaches in small boats People trying to cross the Channel to the UK have reported an increase in French police use of violence on beaches to prevent them from getting into dinghies, according to a French NGO. Utopia 56, which works on beaches from where migrants attempt Channel crossings, says so far this year 2,720 people have reported being victims of French police violence, compared with 1,954 over the same period last year, when crossings overall were much higher. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
